facts.statement: Susisuchus was an extinct crocodyliform that lived in Brazil during the Early Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: Susisuchus is an extinct genus of neosuchian mesoeucrocodylian crocodyliform from the Early Cretaceous of Brazil.

facts.statement: The genus Susisuchus was named in 2003 and is the only member of its family, Susisuchidae.
facts.quote: Named in 2003, Susisuchus is the sole member of the family Susisuchidae, and is closely related to the clade Eusuchia, which includes living crocodilians.

facts.statement: Fossils of Susisuchus have been found in the Nova Olinda Member of the Aptian-age Crato Formation in northeastern Brazil.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found from the Nova Olinda Member of the Aptian-age Crato Formation in the Araripe and Lima Campos Basins of northeastern Brazil.

facts.statement: A second species, S. jaguaribensis, was named in 2009 based on fragmentary remains.
facts.quote: A second species, S. jaguaribensis, was named in 2009 from fragmentary remains.

facts.statement: S. anatoceps was the first crocodyliform described from the Crato Formation in the Araripe Basin.
facts.quote: S. anatoceps was found in the Aptian-age Crato Formation in the Araripe Basin, and was the first crocodyliform to be described from the formation.

facts.statement: Researchers believe the holotype specimen was a desiccated carcass before burial and fossilization.
facts.quote: The specimen is thought to have been a desiccated carcass before it was buried and later fossilized.

facts.statement: The remains of S. jaguaribensis were found about 115 km from the discovery site of S. anatoceps in the Lima Campos Basin.
facts.quote: A second species, S. jaguaribensis, was named in 2009 from the Lima Campos Basin about 115 km from where the skeleton of S. anatoceps was uncovered.

facts.statement: A 2009 specimen from the Crato Formation was tentatively classified as cf. Susisuchus sp. based on unique fibula and leg bone proportions.
facts.quote: A new crocodyliform specimen from the Crato Formation was described in 2009. It can be distinguished from the two other crocodyliforms known from the formation, Araripesuchus and the trematochampsid Caririsuchus, on the basis of characteristics of the fibula and proportions of the femur and tibia.

facts.statement: Both species share a skull feature where the squamosal and parietal bones meet at the posterior border of the supratemporal fenestra.
facts.quote: Both species have a contact between the squamosal and parietal bones that is situated on the posterior border of the supratemporal fenestra, a hole in the skull table.

facts.statement: Susisuchus possesses a dorsal shield of osteoderms similar to those found in modern crocodilians.
facts.quote: Susisuchus has a dorsal shield of osteoderms that is similar to those of the more derived clade Eusuchia, which includes living crocodilians.

facts.statement: Susisuchus was among the first mesoeucrocodylians to evolve a tetraserial paravertebral shield made of dorsal osteoderms.
facts.quote: Susisuchus was one of the first mesoeucrocodylians to have a tetraserial paravertebral shield, which is formed from the dorsal osteoderms to make the back more rigid.

facts.statement: A tetraserial paravertebral shield consists of four separate rows of osteoderms near the midline of the back.
facts.quote: In a tetraserial paravertebral shield, there are four separate rows of paravertebral osteoderms (osteoderms near the midline of the back).

facts.statement: Susisuchus has two rows of accessory osteoderms on either side of the main paravertebral shield.
facts.quote: Susisuchus also has two rows of accessory osteoderms to either side of the paravertebral osteoderms which are not part of the shield.

facts.statement: The segmented paravertebral shield allowed Susisuchus greater lateral flexibility in its trunk.
facts.quote: The segmentation of the paravertebral shield allowed for a greater degree of lateral flexibility in the trunk of Susisuchus.

facts.statement: The flexible shield likely enabled efficient lateral undulation swimming in Susisuchus.
facts.quote: This flexibility would have enabled lateral undulation while swimming, resulting in greater efficiency in locomotion.

facts.statement: Susisuchus was likely restricted to a maximum size of 50 kg because larger bodies would have exceeded the structural limits of its high-walking posture.
facts.quote: However, the ability to high-walk would have restricted the size of Susisuchus. If Susisuchus grew any larger than 50 kg, the forces encountered during high-walking would have been too great for the paravertebral shield to counteract.

facts.statement: Susisuchus is closely related to the genera Pachycheilosuchus and Isisfordia.
facts.quote: Susisuchus is closely related to Pachycheilosuchus from Glen Rose, Texas, United States, and Isisfordia from Winton, Queensland, Australia.

facts.statement: Susisuchus is placed outside the Eusuchia clade as its sister taxon, unlike its relative Isisfordia.
facts.quote: However, with its naming in 2006, Isisfordia was placed within Eusuchia as the most basal member of the clade, while Susisuchus was placed outside Eusuchia as its sister taxon.

facts.statement: Susisuchus possesses amphicoelus vertebrae, meaning the ends of its vertebrae are concave.
facts.quote: Susisuchus has amphicoelus thoracic, lumbar and caudal (tail) vertebrae, meaning that the ends of the centra of these vertebrae are concave.

facts.statement: The combination of amphicoelus vertebrae and a tetraserial shield is unique enough to define the family Susisuchidae.
facts.quote: The presence of this feature in a crocodyliform with a tetraserial paravertebral shield is unusual, and has been used to erect the family Susisuchidae, of which Susisuchus is the only member.

facts.statement: Susisuchus is considered a transitional form, possessing advanced shields but primitive vertebrae.
facts.quote: Susisuchus can be considered a transitional form because it has a tetraserial paravertebral shield characteristic of eusuchians, but retains more primitive amphicoelus vertebrae characteristic of more basal crocodylomorphs.

facts.statement: The genus Susisuchus is now defined as a node-based taxon including the common ancestor of both species and all descendants.
facts.quote: With the description of S. jaguaribensis as a second species of Susisuchus, the genus has been phylogenetically redefined as a node-based taxon including the last common ancestor of Susisuchus anatoceps and Susisuchus jaguaribensis and all of its descendants.

facts.statement: Susisuchus possessed a dorsal shield of osteoderms similar to that of the derived clade Eusuchia, which includes modern crocodilians.
facts.quote: Susisuchus tenía un escudo dorsal de osteodermos que es similar al de los del clado más derivado, Eusuchia que incluye a los crocodilianos actuales.

facts.statement: Susisuchus was one of the first mesoeucrocodylians to have a tetraserial paravertebral shield formed by dorsal osteoderms that made the back more rigid.
facts.quote: Susisuchus fue uno de los primeros mesoeucrocodilianos en tener un escudo tetraserial paravertebral, el cual está formado por los osteodermos dorsales que hacían a la espalda más rígida.

facts.statement: A tetraserial paravertebral shield consists of four separate rows of paravertebral osteoderms located near the midline of the back.
facts.quote: En un escudo tetraserial paravertebral, hay cuatro filas sepradas de osteodermos paravertebrales (osteodermos cercanos a la línea media de la espalda).

facts.statement: In Susisuchus, two rows of large osteoderms segment into four smaller ones.
facts.quote: Hay dos filas de osteodermos grandes que se segmentan en cuatro más pequeños en Susisuchus.

facts.statement: Susisuchus also had two rows of accessory osteoderms on each side of the paravertebral osteoderms, which did not form part of the shield.
facts.quote: Susisuchus además tenía dos filas de osteodermos accesorios a cada lado de los osteodermos paravertebrales, sin formar parte del escudo.

facts.statement: The segmentation of the paravertebral shield allowed for a greater degree of lateral flexibility in the trunk of Susisuchus.
facts.quote: La segmentación del escudo paravertebral permitía un mayor grado de flexibilidad lateral en el tronco de Susisuchus.

facts.statement: This flexibility may have facilitated lateral undulation while swimming, resulting in greater locomotion efficiency.
facts.quote: Esta flexibilidad pudo haber facilitado la ondulación lateral mientras nadaba, resultando en una mayor eficiencia en la locomoción.

facts.statement: Because the width of the paravertebral shield was not compromised by this segmentation, the back could remain rigid enough to withstand forces encountered during upright or semi-upright walking.
facts.quote: Debido a que la anchura del escudo paravertebral no quedaba comprometida por esta segmentación, la espalda podría quedar lo suficientemente rígida como para superar las fuerzas que encontraba durante la caminata erguida, o caminata semierguida.

facts.statement: If Susisuchus grew to a mass exceeding 50 kilograms, the forces encountered during upright walking may have been too large to be counteracted by the paravertebral shield.
facts.quote: Si Susisuchus crecía a una masa superior a los 50 kilogramos, las fuerzas encontradas durante la caminata erguida pueden haber sido demasiado grandes como para ser contrarrestadas por el escudo paravertebral.

facts.statement: Susisuchus is closely related to Pachycheilosuchus from Glen Rose, Texas, USA, and Isisfordia from Winton, Queensland, Australia.
facts.quote: Susisuchus está cercanamente relacionado con Pachycheilosuchus de Glen Rose (Texas), Estados Unidos, e Isisfordia de Winton (Queensland), en Australia.

facts.statement: Susisuchus was placed outside Eusuchia as its sister taxon.
facts.quote: Susisuchus fue situado por fuera de Eusuchia como su taxón hermano.

facts.statement: Susisuchus possessed amphicoelous thoracic, lumbar, and caudal vertebrae, meaning the ends of the centra of these vertebrae were concave.
facts.quote: Susisuchus tenía vértebras torácicas, lumbares y caudales anficélicas, lo que significa que los extremos de los centros de estas vértebras eran cóncavos.

facts.statement: The presence of this trait in a crocodiliform with a tetraserial paravertebral shield is unusual and was used to create the family Susisuchidae, of which Susisuchus is the only member.
facts.quote: La presencia de este rasgo en un crocodiliforme con un escudo tetraserial paravertebral es inusual, y fue usada para la creación de la familia Susisuchidae, de la cual Susisuchus es el único miembro.

facts.statement: Susisuchus can be considered a transitional form because it has a tetraserial paravertebral shield characteristic of eusuchians but retained the amphicoelous vertebrae typical of more basal crocodylomorphs.
facts.quote: Susisuchus puede ser considerado como una forma transicional porque tiene un escudo tetraserial paravertebral característico de los eusuquios, pero conservaba las vértebras anficélicas propias de los crocodilomorfos más basales.

facts.statement: With the description of S. jaguaribensis as a second species, the genus has been redefined phylogenetically as a node-based taxon including the last common ancestor of Susisuchus anatoceps and Susisuchus jaguaribensis and all its descendants.
facts.quote: Con la descripción de S. jaguaribensis como una segunda especie de Susisuchus, el género ha sido redefinido filogenéticamente como un taxón basado en nodos que incluye al último ancestro común de Susisuchus anatoceps y Susisuchus jaguaribensis y a todos sus descendientes.

facts.statement: Susisuchus lived from the Berriasian to the Aptian stages, between 143.1 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Berriasian to Aptian (143.1 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus Susisuchus was named by Salisbury et al. in 2003.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Susisuchus (genus), Salisbury et al. 2003

facts.statement: There are 5 recorded fossil occurrences of Susisuchus.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 5
